subject: Observability add-ons: retention/tracing pricing and SLA trade-offs
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Observability add-ons: retention/tracing pricing and SLA trade-offs

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a short pricing note that shows three paths for observability add-ons (retention, tracing, advanced dashboards):

- Minimal: 30-day retention, basic trace sampling, dashboard seats limited to core team
- Growth: 90-day retention, continuous tracing with sampling tiers, dashboard seats + archived views
- Enterprise: 365-day retention, full tracing retention + replay, unlimited dashboards + hotpath archives

Key questions you raised: how retention affects unit economics, whether tracing can be seatless (metered by spans) and what concession paths exist for pilots.

Attached: redwood-obs-pricing-v1.pdf and a sample workbook you can fill with your expected ingest to see $/month impact.

Would you be open to a short working session this week to run your numbers? I can bring Ben (pricing) and Jordan (commercial) if helpful.

Best,
Sofia
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-obs-pricing-v1.pdf (PDF), acme-maup-retention-workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alex Li <alex.li@acme-analytics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-11-21T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons: retention/tracing pricing and SLA trade-offs

Sofia —

Thanks for the deck and workbook. Couple of questions from our side after a quick pass:

1) For Growth vs Enterprise: it looks like the primary delta is retention days + replay. Can you clarify how that maps to a predictable monthly fee vs a usage surcharge? We need something our procurement team can forecast.
2) Can tracing be billed purely by spans (we have unpredictable bursty spikes)? If not, do you have a hybrid model (seat + spans)?
3) For a pilot (90 days), what concessions / promo credits are realistic? We want to trial advanced dashboards across 10 engineers but we can't commit to Enterprise until we see ROI.

Alex
Head of infra & analytics
Acme Analytics

Date: 2026-11-22T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Observability add-ons: retention/tracing pricing and SLA trade-offs

Looping Jordan and Kimberly into pricing nuance.

High-level thoughts:
- Prefer to keep retention priced as a tiered slab (e.g., 30 / 90 / 365) with an ingestion-band-based surcharge for overage. That gives Acme predictability while protecting us on extreme tail usage.
- For tracing: offer a hybrid — seat-based for replay/archival access + span-metering for ingestion. During pilot we can waive seat fees for up to 10 engineers and cap span ingestion at a negotiated monthly allowance.
- Pilot concession: typical is 3 months free on seat component + 50% off span overage up to a usage cap; require trial success metrics (latency, error surface, retention restore time).

Kimberly — can you draft a short commercial blurb we can send to Alex that lays out the pilot concession + SLA triggers?

Ben
Director, Sales

> On 2026-11-21, Alex Li wrote:
> > (questions on retention mapping and pilot credits)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability add-ons: retention/tracing pricing and SLA trade-offs

Hi team —

Draft commercial summary for Acme below. Feel free to edit before I send.

---
Commercial summary (draft):
Pilot offer (90 days)
- Advanced Dashboards: seats for up to 10 engineers waived for pilot period (no seat fees)
- Tracing: span ingestion allowance of 75M spans/month included; 50% discount on span overage up to 150M spans/month; seat fees for replay/archive waived for pilot
- Retention: Growth tier (90-day) enabled for pilot. If ingestion exceeds Growth slab, overage billed at tiered rate (see attached workbook).
- SLA & success metrics: 99.5% dashboard availability during pilot; <200ms median dashboard load; tracing retention restore within SLA window for Enterprise conversion consideration.

Conversion guidance:
- If ACME converts to an annual Growth commitment: 12% discount on combined observability add-ons vs list.
- If ACME commits to Enterprise 12-month: 20% discount on list + onboarding credit.

Required sign-off: PO or signed SOW; pilot begins on receipt of PO or countersigned SOW.
---

I'll send this to Alex once you approve.

Kim
Head of Commercial Operations
From: Alex Li <alex.li@acme-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability add-ons: retention/tracing pricing and SLA trade-offs

Thanks Kimberly — this is helpful and clearer. A few follow-ups before we loop procurement:

- Can you convert the Growth tier to a fixed monthly fee (we'll provide expected ingest numbers in the attached workbook). If not fully possible, give us an example invoice for three different ingest scenarios so procurement can model it.
- For the pilot span allowance — can you include a one-time grace for the first burst month (we expect initial onboarding spikes)?
- Can you add a short sentence on data residency (we need EU residency for a subset later) and whether the pilot can be regionally isolated?

If you can update the SOW to reflect the pilot concession and the grace period, we'll route to procurement next week.

Alex

Alex —

Appreciate the quick turn. We're aligned on pilot concessions. Action items and responses below: 

1) Fixed-fee example invoices: Jordan will produce three invoice scenarios (low / expected / high ingest) using your updated workbook; we'll attach a worked example to the SOW.
2) Onboarding burst: happy to include a one-time onboarding grace (first month) that waives span overage charges up to an extra 50% of the monthly allowance. We'll note this in the SOW.
3) Data residency: pilot can be regionally isolated to us-west (for now); EU residency is supported for Enterprise rollouts — we'll include a short clause in the SOW describing timeline and cost delta for EU residency.

Next steps: Jordan to attach worked invoice examples; Kimberly to update SOW and send final countersign-ready doc. Can we target EOD Friday for the updated SOW so you can route to procurement next week?

Thanks — sending updated SOW and sample invoice is on our side.

Best,
Sofia
